name: assistant-runtime-adapter-registry
purpose: Maps shared workspace operating principles to AI coding assistant runtimes such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, and generic tools.

reader_guide.summary: Open this file when using this repository with an AI coding tool other than Codex, or when adding a new runtime-specific instruction adapter.
how_to_read: Read canonical_policy_paths first to see which files define durable behavior.
Read structure_rules to understand what must stay shared and what may be runtime-specific.
Read runtimes to find the instruction files or rule directories each tool should use.
Add a new runtime only when a real tool needs a different instruction loading mechanism.
Run config contract and structure audit checks after changing this file or runtime adapter directories.
update_triggers: A new AI coding assistant runtime is introduced.
A runtime changes its project instruction file or rule directory behavior.
The shared operating model moves or changes scope.
A runtime-specific adapter directory is added at repository root.
A runtime-specific rule starts duplicating shared policy instead of linking to it.

structure_rules.rule: Durable behavior belongs in shared policy files first; runtime-specific files should import, reference, or summarize those policies.
structure_rules.reason: The same workspace should work from Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, or another tool without policy drift.

structure_rules.rule: Runtime adapters should contain only loading instructions, activation hints, and runtime-specific caveats.
structure_rules.reason: Duplicating full policy in multiple tool formats creates contradictions and maintenance overhead.

structure_rules.rule: If a runtime cannot enforce a repository rule directly, record the limitation and rely on verification, settings, hooks, approvals, or human review.
structure_rules.reason: Prompt instructions shape model behavior but do not guarantee enforcement across tools.

structure_rules.rule: Tracked root runtime adapter directories must be listed in root-structure-policy.json runtime_adapter_dirs.
structure_rules.reason: Dot-directories should not bypass root folder ownership and audit rules.

structure_rules.rule: Reusable templates must avoid hard-coding one assistant vendor unless the file is explicitly an adapter template.
structure_rules.reason: The user wants the workspace principles to remain usable with the tool they prefer.

field_guide.meaning: Shared files that define durable workspace behavior independently of runtime.
Tracked files and directories used to load shared rules in specific AI coding tools.
Runtime-specific instruction entrypoints, adapter paths, caveats, and setup notes.
Rules explaining that prompts are not hard enforcement and must be backed by verification where needed.
Commands to run after changing this registry or runtime adapter files.

runtimes.name: OpenAI Codex
setup_notes: This repository currently uses AGENTS.md as the active top-level instruction file.
Keep Codex-specific workflow details in AGENTS.md only when they are actual runtime behavior; shared rules should also be reflected in the tool-agnostic operating model.
caveats: Codex-specific tool names and sandbox behavior should not be copied blindly into other runtime adapters.

runtimes.name: Claude Code
setup_notes: CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md and adds Claude Code adapter notes.
Use .claude/rules for scoped Claude Code rules when the common policy becomes too large or path-specific.
caveats: Claude Code documentation treats CLAUDE.md as context, not a hard enforcement layer; critical rules still need verification commands or settings.

runtimes.name: Cursor
setup_notes: Use .cursor/rules for versioned project rules and AGENTS.md as the simple shared instruction source.
Use Always or scoped rule activation depending on the rule size and path specificity.
caveats: Cursor rule application depends on rule metadata, scope, and activation type; keep important repository-wide behavior in an always-applied adapter.

runtimes.name: Google Antigravity
setup_notes: Use .agents/rules for workspace rules and set the operating-principles rule to Always On when configuring Antigravity.
Prefer New Worktree Mode for isolated concurrent work when a task is complex or parallel.
caveats: Project settings and permissions are runtime controls; Markdown rules should describe behavior but not replace security settings.

runtimes.name: Generic AI coding assistant
setup_notes: Use the shared principles template as the source document.
Create a thin adapter in the target tool's preferred rule format.
caveats: Unknown tools must be treated as prompt-only until their file loading, permission, and sandbox behavior are verified.

capability_boundaries: Instruction files provide persistent context but are not equivalent to sandbox, permission, or policy enforcement.
Critical rules such as secret handling, destructive command avoidance, and publish/push behavior should be backed by repository checks, tool settings, or explicit human review.
When a runtime lacks a feature, document the gap and use the nearest available verification mechanism instead of pretending the capability exists.
